title: An ample module has positive Hilbert degree on a proper scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a nonempty proper $k$-scheme of dimension $g$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module in the sense of [def-sc-ample]. Then the Hilbert degree $\deg_{\mathcal L}(X)$ of [def-sc-hilbert-degree] is positive.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 0BEV (label lemma-ample-positive), with Definition 33.45.3 (label definition-intersection-number): the self-intersection $(\mathcal L^g\cdot X)$ is the Hilbert degree

proof.text: If $g=0$, apply [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ (whose support is $X$ of dimension $0$) and $\mathcal N=\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$. It gives $\chi(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes m})=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=\dim_k\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and this dimension is at least $1$ because $X$ is nonempty; hence the degree is positive.

source.place: Tag 0BEV, induction on d, base case d=0, using Tag 0AYT

proof.text: For $g>0$, [lem-sc-top-dimensional-reduction-intersection] (Tag 0BES) reduces the top self-intersection on $X$ to the sum, with positive generic multiplicities, of the self-intersections on the integral top-dimensional components $Z_i$. Each $Z_i$ is a closed subscheme of $X$, hence proper over $k$ of dimension $g$, and $\mathcal L|_{Z_i}$ is ample in the sense of [def-sc-ample]: choose $r\ge1$ with $\mathcal L^{\otimes r}$ very ample, giving a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ with $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L^{\otimes r}$; the composite closed immersion $Z_i\hookrightarrow X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ pulls $\mathcal O(1)$ back to $\mathcal L^{\otimes r}|_{Z_i}$, which is therefore ample by [lem-pc-very-ample-ample]; so some power $\mathcal L^{\otimes rm}|_{Z_i}$ is very ample and $\mathcal L|_{Z_i}$ is ample by [def-sc-ample]. Thus it is enough to prove positivity after replacing $X$ by an integral proper component of dimension $g$ and $\mathcal L$ by its restriction.

source.place: Tag 0BEV proof, reduction to the integral case via Tag 0BES and restriction of ampleness to a closed subscheme

proof.text: Write $P(m)=\chi(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$ and let $Q$ be the Hilbert polynomial supplied by [lem-sc-hilbert-polynomial], so $P(m)=Q(m)$. By [def-sc-intersection-number], $(\mathcal L^g\cdot X)$ is the coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_g$ in $Q(n_1+\cdots+n_g)$. If $Q(t)=a_g t^g+\cdots$, then the only contribution to that squarefree monomial comes from $a_g(n_1+\cdots+n_g)^g$, whose coefficient is $g!$; hence $(\mathcal L^g\cdot X)=g!a_g$. Once positivity is established below, this forces $a_g>0$, so $\deg Q=g$ and [def-sc-hilbert-degree] gives $\deg_{\mathcal L}(X)=g!a_g=(\mathcal L^g\cdot X)$. Replacing $\mathcal L$ by a positive tensor power replaces $Q(m)$ by $Q(rm)$ and multiplies both sides by $r^g$, so positivity is unchanged.

source.place: Tag 0BEV proof together with Definition Tag 0BEP and the remark after Definition Tag 0BEW

proof.text: By [def-sc-ample], choose $r\ge1$ such that $\mathcal L^{\otimes r}$ is very ample, giving a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ with $i^*\mathcal O(1)=\mathcal L^{\otimes r}$. Since $X$ is nonempty, some coordinate $x_j$ has $i(X)$ not contained in $V(x_j)$. The section $s=i^*x_j$ has nonempty nonvanishing locus $X_s=i^{-1}(D_+(x_j))$, a nonempty closed subscheme of the affine $D_+(x_j)\cong\mathbf A^N_k$, hence affine. Replacing $\mathcal L$ by this power is allowed by the preceding step.

source.place: Tag 0BEV (lemma-ample-positive), choose a power and a section with affine principal open

proof.text: The integral proper scheme $X$ of positive dimension cannot itself be affine: if it were, the proper-and-affine finiteness criterion would make $X$ finite over the field, hence $0$-dimensional. Therefore the complement $D:=X\setminus X_s=Z(s)$ is nonempty.

The section $s$ is nonzero because $X_s$ is nonempty. On the integral scheme, its zero scheme $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor by the nonzero-section criterion. Tag 0BEU gives that $D$ is proper of dimension $g-1$, that the restricted module remains ample, and that $(\mathcal L^g\cdot X)=(\mathcal L^{g-1}\cdot D)$.

source.place: Tag 0BEV (lemma-ample-positive), using Tag 0BEU and the nonzero-section Cartier fact

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis to the nonempty proper scheme $D$ of dimension $g-1$ with its restricted ample module. The equality in the preceding step then makes $(\mathcal L^g\cdot X)$ positive, completing the induction and hence the Hilbert-degree inequality.

source.place: Tag 0BEV (lemma-ample-positive), final application of the induction hypothesis
